title: That's Not the Ocean in a Seashell #science #sound
description:
That's not the ocean in a seashell. It's the noise of the room around you. The shell's hollow inside resonates, so some pitches ring louder than others, like blowing across a bottle, and the mix sounds like waves. In a noisy cafe the 'ocean' gets louder; in a very quiet room it fades to a faint hush. An empty cup does it too.

More about sound: How do headphones cancel noise with more noise? https://youtu.be/rOxQ3PFvewk

Sources
- Library of Congress, Everyday Mysteries: Can you hear the ocean in a seashell? (loc.gov)
- Kinsler, L. E. et al., Fundamentals of Acoustics (Wiley), chapter on cavity (Helmholtz) resonators
- The spectrum bars in the animation are schematic

Did you believe it was the ocean as a kid?

Script, voice and animation are AI-produced (Claude; Kokoro voice). Every claim is checked against the sources above.
